correctness.rationale: With the source definition, singular Gamma 1-cubes correspond exactly to ordered distinct pairs in a common hyperedge, and the antisymmetrization map onto simplicial C1 has kernel generated by reversals. Each reversal is the boundary of the admissible Gamma 2-cube (a,b,a,a). The four images a,b,c,d of any Gamma 2-cube yield opposite-star simplicial triangles (a,b,c) and (b,d,c), whose summed oriented boundaries are exactly the antisymmetrized Gamma boundary. Conversely (a,b,c,b) realizes the oriented triangle boundary for any simplex (a,b,c), establishing equality of image-boundary lattices and the H1 isomorphism over Z without rational-only steps. Degree zero and naturality follow from compatible vertex and edge boundaries. For the ten-triple six-vertex surface, every edge occurs twice, each vertex link is a five-cycle, chi=1, and the integral d2 Smith diagonal is 1 repeated nine times then 2, while rank d1=5, yielding H1=Z/2. The standalone checker tests 25,427 source-admissible 2-cubes and the exact projective-plane boundary matrices. Higher degrees not claimed.

value.rationale: A universal functorial comparison, valid over the integers for every covered-vertex finite hypergraph, determines the entire first Gamma homology and its persistence without re-enumerating higher singular cubes. This clarifies the information content of a new theory, yields a genuine integral two-torsion hypergraph example using the canonical six-vertex projective-plane triangulation, and distinguishes the Gamma invariant from embedded homology. The exact object-wide result and torsion mechanism have intrinsic computational and conceptual value, despite the short chain-level proof.
